resolutions.reproduced: Yes, both directions, exactly as reported. FALSE GREEN: `deepLink();` moved into the catch arm (`}catch(e){ $("#sha").textContent = "meta unavailable"; deepLink(); }`) gave `[PASS] ui-deep-link`, invariant 63/63 = 1.000, with the deep link running only when /api/meta fails. FALSE RED: the whole `function deepLink(){…}` declaration hoisted above `async function boot(){` — behaviour-identical, declarations hoist — gave `[FAIL] ui-deep-link`, 62/63 = 0.984, `out of order: 'if(!want || ![...$("#fx").options].some(o => o.value === want)) return;' (@15053) runs before 'deepLink();' (@15416)`.
resolutions.route_taken: Acceptance route 1 (containment), not the reduced-scope route. Route 2 as written does not satisfy the acceptance's own final sentence: reducing `order` to the options-assignment -> call-site pair leaves mutation (a) GREEN, because the call site is still textually after the options assignment when it sits inside the catch arm. Containment is the only one of the two offered mechanisms that makes (a) red. No third mechanism was invented.
resolutions.fix: All ordering machinery is deleted from check_deep_link — no `order` input, no `flat.find()` comparison, no `deep_link_order` info key. The call site is pinned by CONTAINMENT instead: `wire`'s first entry is one contiguous span running from the `$("#fx").innerHTML = m.fixtures…` assignment, through the `}catch(e){…}` arm, to `deepLink();`. Any relocation out of `boot()`'s straight-line tail — into the catch arm, ahead of the fetch, or anywhere else — is simply a missing pin, and the span also covers the options assignment being moved away from in front of it. The standalone pins for those two expressions were dropped as redundant, so `wire` is 6 pins. The docstring no longer claims the guard's or run trigger's position means anything, because it does not: both live inside the function body, whose textual position says nothing about when it runs.
